NextItNet’s foundation is stacked causal dilated convolutions with residual connections, increasing receptive fields without pooling; its implementation uses channel-wise layer normalization and left-only convolution padding ([paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf), [implementation](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html)). Relevant recent work supports adaptive interest aggregation, although the retrieved sources do not establish the exact proposed NextItNet extension. ScaleRec (January 2026) models multiple temporal granularities, separates transient interests from stable preferences, and uses context-adaptive aggregation plus adaptive masking ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2025.104318)). HGNCDSR (2025) applies feature-level and instance-level gates to extract interests, but addresses cross-domain recommendation rather than causal dilation selection ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3715321)).

Design inference: retain one jointly trained NextItNet backbone and aggregate normalized intermediate residual-block states using a per-position softmax gate. Condition gate logits on the current causal state, a masked prefix summary, and observed prefix length; different block depths provide different receptive fields, allowing history-dependent emphasis on recent intent versus persistent interests. Keep the final residual path to preserve a direct predictive representation. Padding safety requires explicitly zeroing padded states after normalization and residual updates, excluding padding from prefix summaries, and preventing all-padding softmax cases. Compute gates only from the available prefix; read out the final nonpadding position, never count-minus-one for left-padded histories. Treat this as an experimental synthesis, with uniform aggregation and final-block-only readout as useful ablations; the cited papers do not establish its effectiveness or padding behavior.

Strong sampled separation does not establish useful top-K ranking. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) found sampler performance depends on dataset popularity structure: random negatives favored head items, while popularity-based sampling improved balance at an overall accuracy cost. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) revises sampled-softmax importance correction because the positive is always included, rather than sampled. Its uncertainty-weighted formulation is relevant to multi-negative training; sampling-distribution correction does not itself identify false negatives.

[R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) provides a practical curriculum: uniform-negative warm-up, efficient global candidate recall, then stochastic selection from a progressively narrower top-M pool.
